definition: The Akan supreme being, also called Nyankopon, associated with the sky. Nyame is often distant from daily life, and prayers are carried to him through the abosom and the ancestors.
The Akan earth goddess, whose name means Earth Yaa, since Yaa is the day-name for a Thursday-born girl. She receives the dead, gives fertility, and is honoured with libation.
The spider trickster of Akan folktales, clever, greedy and comic. His name is preserved in anansesem, the Akan term for stories, and in Anansi tales told across the Caribbean.
The sacred stool of the Asante nation, called Sika Dwa Kofi. It is understood as the soul of the nation rather than a seat, is never sat upon, and is treated with great respect.
A powerful Akan state and later empire centred on Kumasi, in present-day Ghana. The Asante union was founded around 1700 under Osei Tutu and Okomfo Anokye.
Akan lesser gods or powers, often associated with rivers, rocks, trees and other places. They stand between the supreme being and people, and receive offerings at their shrines.
A flat-headed wooden doll carried by Akan women hoping to conceive, and by girls learning to care for children. The name means Akua's child, after the woman in the origin story.
A monstrous creature of the Akan deep forest, said to hang from the highest trees and to have iron teeth and red eyes. It marks the dangerous edge of the settled world.

Akan symbols stamped on cloth and printed on buildings, each standing for a proverb or a saying. Adinkra cloth is worn at funerals and on important occasions, and the motifs let a message be worn rather than spoken.
A woven Akan cloth of bright, narrow strips, made famous by Asante weavers. Patterns have names and meanings, and kente is worn for festivals, weddings and important ceremonies.
